title: Proton therapy of brain tumors: Prospective collection of effectiveness and side effects with standard clinical doses
summary:
Radiotherapy with protons has compared to standard radiotherapy with photons the physical advantage of a lower burden of the surrounding healthy tissue with middle and low radiation doses. Whether this also leads to an advantage for adult patients with brain tumors in terms of side effects of radiotherapy has not been sufficiently investigated yet. 

The main objective of the study is the investigation of proton therapy in terms of side effects. Patients with brain tumors where radiotherapy with the objective of healing (or long-term tumor control) is indicated, receive a proton therapy with total doses and fractionation schemes similar to the standard photon therapy. A simultaneous chemotherapy is administered as clinically indicated analogous to photon therapy.
conditions: Benign neoplasm of brain and other parts of central nervous system

interventions.name: Primary brain tumors (radiotherapy with protons; 2.0 Gy / Fx, total dose 54-60 Gy)
Postoperative brain tumors (radiotherapy with protons; 2.0 Gy / Fx, total dose 54-60 Gy)
Recurrent brain tumors (radiotherapy with protons; 2.0 to 5 Gy / Fx, total dose of 30-50 Gy)
Glioblastomas in patients >70 years (radiotherapy with protons; moderate hypofractionated 2.67 to 40 Gy (RBE))

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- brain tumor: gliomas (low or high grade), meningiomas, pituitary adenoma, craniopharyngiomas and other rare brain tumors and AV malformations
- Age >= 18 years old
- ECOG > 2
- Indication for high-dose radiotherapy or radiochemotherapy
 - Capacity to consent and written consent of the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to consent or lack of written consent of the patient
- Inability to MRI planning (eg. contraindications to performing MRI)
- Lack of compliance of the patient
- Lack of or limited possibility of a reproducible storage (eg by severe restriction of mobility of the patient)
